2607.21552.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
2607.21552.paper_summary: Unlike large language models (LLMs) that exhibit strong reasoning capabilities, vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with visual reasoning, even on geometry problems that admit equivalent text, diagram, and combined diagram+text views. We show that these views often elicit different behaviors: a model may solve a problem from text but fail on the corresponding diagram, or succeed visually while failing textually. This inconsistency suggests that different views expose complementary reasoning paths and failure modes that standard multimodal post-training does not fully exploit. To study and exploit this phenomenon, we construct ODA-Data, a high-quality paired multimodal geometry dataset with text-dominant, image-dominant, and combined image+text views of the same problems, together with splits for training and evaluating modality-dependent reasoning behaviors. We then develop Modality-Informed Reciprocal Reasoning Optimization (MIRROR), a reinforcement learning approach for improving multimodal reasoning via self supervision. For each problem, MIRROR evaluates the model under all views, selects the best-performing view as a teacher, and trains other views with a reverse-KL objective towards the teacher. Across reasoning benchmarks that evaluate on geometry problems, MIRROR improves over standard RL and yields more accurate and consistent behavior across modalities
2607.21552.paper_summary_zh: 與展現強大推理能力的大型語言模型（LLMs）不同，視覺-語言模型（VLMs）在視覺推理方面表現不佳，即使在允許等效文本、圖表和結合圖表+文本視圖的幾何問題上。我們顯示這些視圖經常引發不同的行為：一個模型可能從文本中解決問題，但在相應的圖表上失敗，或者在視覺上成功而在文本上失敗。這種不一致性表明，不同的視圖揭示了互補的推理路徑和失敗模式，而標準的多模態後訓練並未充分利用這些模式。為了研究和利用這一現象，我們構建了ODA-Data，一個高質量的配對多模態幾何數據集，包含文本主導、圖像主導和相同問題的結合圖像+文本視圖，並為訓練和評估模態依賴的推理行為提供了劃分。我們接著開發了模態知情的互惠推理優化（MIRROR），這是一種通過自我監督來改善多模態推理的強化學習方法。對於每個問題，MIRROR在所有視圖下評估模型，選擇表現最佳的視圖作為教師，並以反向KL目標訓練其他視圖。在評估幾何問題的推理基準中，MIRROR在標準強化學習上有所改進，並在各模態之間產生更準確和一致的行為。
